purpose: What the product is, who it is for and how you will know it is working. Every other file defers to it on those three questions.
The rules for how the product looks, reads and behaves: visual system, UX principles, components, forms and accessibility. Anything a check could enforce lives here.
readNote: /ux-os:init offers it as a house rule, and /ux-os:run then holds third-party skills to it.

purpose: The first file an AI coding agent reads: a pointer to the guides, plus the few rules that must not be missed. Never a second copy of the guide.
readNote: Most coding agents look for AGENTS.md by convention. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, so have one point at the other.

purpose: Who the product is for, as people with situations, goals and frustrations. Beliefs until research backs them.
readNote: The ux-os research skills read it as beliefs once .research-profile.md lists it under Belief files.

purpose: How each primary persona gets the job done today, stage by stage, with where it hurts. Beliefs until research backs them.
readNote: The ux-os research skills read it as beliefs once .research-profile.md lists it under Belief files.

purpose: The progress people are trying to make, independent of any product, and what they hire to make it today. Beliefs until research backs them.
readNote: The ux-os research skills read it as beliefs once .research-profile.md lists it under Belief files.

purpose: The judgment no check can enforce: what to reason toward and away from, what reads as machine-made, and the kill list. DESIGN.md says what is allowed; this says what is good.
How things move: the feel in three words, the standard values as tokens, the allowed patterns, the banned ones and the reduced-motion rule.
How the product sounds in every word a user reads: the voice in one line, pillars with before and after, words to avoid and the shape of common messages.
readNote: No skill reads VOICE.md by name yet. /ux-os:init offers it as a house rule, so point AGENTS.md at it.
